items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1959-09-25
items.q: Ricard was turning out to be a nice trumpet player too until he got hype.

ctx.x: Well, let me get out my little notebook again, Punch, and we'll go back and I'll ask you about some of the different people and bands you work with, stuff like that. I wanted to ask you more about the different styles of the trumpet players they had here. Like, how would you describe Buddy Petit's style?

Well, I'm telling you, he had a wonderful style of playing at home. He wasn't a high note man, but he was, he had a wonderful tone and played everything clean. Real clean trumpet player. He was. Rene, he was a high note man. He went up in the air all the time. Ricard was turning out to be a nice trumpet player too until he got hype. Ricard was getting all right. What about Chris Kelly?

items.title: Ernest "Punch" Miller Interview, 1959-08-20
items.q: Either him or Ricard, I can't remember which.

ctx.x: Oh, let me see who he is. At least no shots come after me. That was an old man, I forget who it was now. But shots come after me you know. Didn't I think I killed after shots eh?

Either him or Ricard, I can't remember which. They were both in there and I can never remember which is which. So let's see, you were in the army and who were some of the other New Orleans guys in the army with you?

Well, just Oscar Shields. There was about the three of us, oh no, what is I'm talking about? Clowns Todd, Chiff, there's a triumphant player named Ben. Ben, Ben something, he from off the river to a real Creole fellow. Ben, he named Ben, I can't think of his first name.
